subChunks.title: Tables, Rows, and Columns
subChunks.hookHtml: Every fact the Academy has ever recorded — every apprentice, every quest, every grade — lives in a table. Before you write a single query, you must learn to read one.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
What a table is

A table is a grid. Rows are records — one row per entity. Columns are attributes — one column per named piece of information. A table called apprentices might hold:

id | name    | rank        | xp
---+---------+-------------+------
 1 | Alice   | Apprentice  | 1200
 2 | Bjorn   | Adept       | 2400
 3 | Cassia  | Mage        | 4800

Columns have types

id and xp are integers; name and rank are text. The type determines which comparisons make sense. xp > 2000 is valid; name > 2000 is nonsense — you cannot compare text to a number meaningfully.

Key vocabulary

  • Schema — the column names + types that define a table's structure
  • Primary key — a column whose value uniquely identifies each row (almost always called id)
  • NULL — the absence of a value. Not the same as 0 or empty string.

Reading a schema

When you see quests(id INT, title TEXT NOT NULL, xp INT, difficulty TEXT), think: a quest has an id, a required title, optional xp, optional difficulty. That instinct drives every query you will ever write.

storyBeats.text: You descend into the Academy's Hall of Records. Shelves stretch into the dim distance, packed with leather-bound ledgers.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: Each ledger is a table. Every row is one thing — one apprentice, one quest. Every column is one fact about it. The types tell you which questions make sense. Read the schema first — always.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
📜 Read the schema

Study the apprentices schema below. In your own words, explain: what does each column store, which column is the primary key, and why WHERE name > 1000 is a type error.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
-- apprentices schema:
-- id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
-- name TEXT    NOT NULL
-- rank TEXT    NOT NULL
-- xp   INTEGER NOT NULL

-- Sample data:
-- id | name    | rank        | xp
--  1 | Alice   | Apprentice  | 1200
--  2 | Bjorn   | Adept       | 2400
--  3 | Cassia  | Mage        | 4800
--  4 | Dorian  | Novice      |   80
subChunks.guidedPracticeModelAnswer: The `id` column is the primary key — it uniquely identifies each apprentice. `name` and `rank` store text; `xp` stores a whole number (integer). `WHERE name > 1000` is a type error because `name` is TEXT — you cannot compare text to a number with a greater-than operator in a meaningful way. The correct comparison for text is equality: `WHERE name = 'Alice'`.
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml:
🏹 Schema analysis

Write a short paragraph identifying: the primary key of the quests table below, which columns are nullable, and one query that would be a type error.

quests(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, xp INTEGER, difficulty TEXT)
subChunks.modelAnswer: The primary key is `id` — it uniquely identifies each quest. `xp` and `difficulty` are nullable (no NOT NULL constraint), meaning a quest can exist without a known XP reward or difficulty rating. `title` is required (NOT NULL). A type error example: `WHERE title > 50` — comparing a TEXT column to an integer.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain to a complete beginner what a database table is, what a row and column mean, and why columns having types matters. Use the apprentices table as your example.

questions.prompt: In a SQL table, what is a row?
options: One record — one entity with values for every column
One named attribute shared by all records
A type definition like INTEGER or TEXT
questions.answer: One record — one entity with values for every column
questions.explanation: A row is one entity (one apprentice, one quest). A column is the named attribute (e.g. xp). Rows and columns together form the table grid.

options: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row
The first column in the table
A column that cannot be NULL
questions.answer: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row
questions.explanation: The primary key uniquely identifies each row — no two rows can share the same primary key value. It is almost always named `id`.

questions.prompt: Given apprentices(id INTEGER, name TEXT, xp INTEGER), which WHERE clause is a type error?
questions.explanation: `name` is TEXT — comparing it to 500 (an integer) with `>` is a type error. You can compare text with `=` or `LIKE`, but not with numeric comparisons against integer literals.

questions.prompt: Two apprentices describe NULL. Who is correct?
options: 'NULL is the absence of a value — distinct from 0 or empty string'
'NULL is just another way to write zero'
'NULL means the column was left empty, same as an empty string'
'NULL is an error state — the row should be deleted'
questions.answer: 'NULL is the absence of a value — distinct from 0 or empty string'
questions.explanation: NULL means the value is unknown or not applicable — it is not 0 (a known integer) and not '' (a known empty string). This distinction becomes critical when filtering with IS NULL vs = ''.
